## Conclusion

I have sufficient evidence. The working replicaset has `memory: 128Mi` limits while the crashing one has `memory: 8Mi`.

```
ROOT CAUSE: Deployment resource limits were incorrectly reduced from 128Mi to 8Mi memory, causing Python containers to be OOMKilled immediately on startup.

EVIDENCE:
  - kubectl describe pod demo-app-854bcdf87-nbrff -> Last State: Terminated, Reason: OOMKilled, Exit Code: 137
  - kubectl logs demo-app-854bcdf87-nbrff --previous -> no output (killed before logging)
  - kubectl get rs demo-app-54bdb6474c -o jsonpath (working) -> {"limits":{"cpu":"200m","memory":"128Mi"},"requests":{"cpu":"20m","memory":"48Mi"}}
  - kubectl get rs demo-app-854bcdf87 -o jsonpath (crashing) -> {"limits":{"cpu":"100m","memory":"8Mi"},"requests":{"cpu":"10m","memory":"8Mi"}}
  - kubectl get deploy demo-app -o yaml -> current spec has 8Mi but last-applied-configuration shows 128Mi

CONFIDENCE: high

PROPOSED PATCH:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: demo-app
  namespace: rca-test
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: 200m
            memory: 128Mi
          requests:
            cpu: 20m
            memory: 48Mi
```
